html:
SMTO-FIL-0048 — A skip list in this folder is too large for SMTO to read

GUID: b838fbb3-9ec7-44da-9dca-7f6a73767801
Slug: file-ignore-limit
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • While looking through the folder, SMTO found a list of files to skip (such as a .gitignore file) that is bigger than 64 KB. It couldn't use that list, so the results are marked incomplete.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to search or list a smaller folder that doesn't contain the oversized .gitignore, .ignore or .rgignore file. SMTO only reads skip lists up to 64 KB, so leaving that file out lets the scan finish cleanly.
  2. If you want every file included anyway, tell SMTO not to use skip lists such as .gitignore for this search. Without skip lists, SMTO doesn't need to read the oversized file at all.
  3. If the oversized file is yours, make it smaller than 64 KB, for example by removing repeated or unused lines. Once the file is small enough, SMTO can read it and apply its rules again.

What success looks like

  • SMTO's answer no longer says the results are incomplete, and the files you expected are listed.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't treat the earlier results as a full list; some skip rules were not applied.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Walker.rules skipped an ignore file (.gitignore, .ignore or .rgignore) larger than 65,536 bytes and marked the traversal incomplete with reason ignore_limit.

What this means

  • A traversal ignore file exceeds 65,536 bytes and cannot be loaded into the bounded rule parser. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A traversal ignore file exceeds 65,536 bytes and cannot be loaded into the bounded rule parser.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect traversal completeness and the exact ignore file's size before relying on search/list results.

How to fix it

  • Find the oversized ignore file in the errors list of the traversal result. Narrow the traversal root, repeat the call with respect_ignore set to false, or reduce the ignore file below 64 KiB; treat the earlier result as incomplete because those rules were not applied.
  • Narrow the traversal or simplify the intended ignore file deliberately. Inspect traversal completeness before relying on the results; do not assume omitted ignore rules were applied.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported bounded rule file is read and traversal reports its actual completeness.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
